classification.difficultyReason: Interpret 'does not use the train', select the four Train regions or the four exterior regions, and convert the resulting count to a probability using 180. The complete diagram supports a routine counting-to-fraction sequence.

content.prompt:
A council surveyed 180 residents about the transport they use to get to work. The results are recorded in the Venn diagram below.

If one of the residents is selected at random, what is the probability that the resident does not use the train?

spec.description: Rectangular universal-set frame containing three intersecting circles: Bus (top), Train (bottom left) and Bike (bottom right). Every region carries a printed count. No universal-set label.
spec.mathematics: Bus only 34; Train only 27; Bike only 21; Bus and Train only 14; Bus and Bike only 11; Train and Bike only 9; all three 6; outside all sets 58. Total 34+27+21+14+11+9+6+58 = 180.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied region counts appear. The probability is withheld.

answer.worked: $\begin{aligned}\text{Residents who use the train} &= 27+14+9+6=56\\\text{Residents who do not use the train} &= 180-56=124\\P(\text{does not use the train}) &= \frac{124}{180}=\frac{31}{45}\end{aligned}$
